$.toolUseResult.annotations.1 — Where does a watcher choose their level?

INF-1554 puts a Watch / Watching toggle and the watcher avatars in the project page header. This project adds two levels per project ("Deficiencies & escalations", the default, and "Everything") plus a weekly digest opt-in. Company settings are admin-only, so members have no settings page today.

A) The Watching button opens a small menu: the two levels as radio choices, a weekly-digest checkbox, and Stop watching. Everything is on the project you're looking at, as on GitHub and Linear. Email footer links land on the same choices.
B) Watch stays a plain toggle. A new "My notifications" page lists every project you watch with a level dropdown each. It needs a new nav item and route.

I recommend A. Subtraction default: the choice lives where the project is, adds no page, and the footer links cover "change it from my inbox". B can come later if people watch dozens of projects.

$.toolUseResult.annotations.2 — Do the email-footer confirm pages need sign-in?

The footer links (Change level, Stop watching, Watch this project) go through /r/<trigger_id> to a confirm page that acts only on a button press (a POST), so link scanners change nothing. The trigger_id already says who the email went to. Sign-in today is email, then password or a 6-digit code.

A) No sign-in for Stop watching and Change level. A public page (the counterparty-share NeutralScreen look) says "Stop watching Riverside Tower for jim@acme.com?" [Stop watching], and acts on that recipient only. Watch this project goes through normal Portal sign-in, because it adds the person to a project.
B) Every confirm page is in the Portal behind sign-in.

I recommend A. Turning mail down should take one click, the way unsubscribe always does. Making someone sign in to get fewer emails is how emails end up marked as spam. The worst a forwarded email can do is stop someone watching or lower their level, which is low-harm, undoable from the header, and logged. Adding someone as a watcher is a membership change, so it needs a real session.

$.toolUseResult.annotations.3 — What does the weekly summary do in a quiet week?

The digest is one email per watcher, sent Monday morning in the org's timezone. It lists their opted-in projects with last week's changes, grouped by project. Every digest sent is a ledger row, and ledger rows are the denominator of the Staples adoption number.

A) Skip the week when none of your projects changed. No email and no ledger row.
B) Always send. A quiet week says "No changes on your 3 projects this week" and gives a status line per project.

I recommend A. An email that says nothing teaches people to ignore the ones that matter. It would also add triggers no one has a reason to act on, which drags adoption down for a reason that isn't real. The ledger still records that the digest was checked and skipped (a run-level log line, not a recipient row), so the gap check can tell "nothing to say" from "failed to send".

$.toolUseResult.annotations.4 — Does someone added as a watcher by a colleague (or a broker in Lens) hear about it?

Under INF-1554 any member can add any other member. Sara is added by Jim and is set to "Deficiencies & escalations". Her first email from Riverside Tower might be weeks later, an escalation with no context.

A) Send Sara one short email right away: "Jim Moore added you as a watcher on Riverside Tower. You'll get emails when something there needs attention." It has an [Open Riverside Tower] button and the usual footer (Everything · Stop watching). It is a ledger row of kind `watch_added`, which the Staples reporting project can count or leave out. Adding yourself sends nothing.
B) Nothing is sent. Sara finds out from her first real notice, whose footer explains why she got it.

I recommend A. Trust is earned at the pixel level: mail you didn't ask for, from a sender you can't place, reads as spam. One line naming who added her, with a one-click way out, avoids that. It also catches a wrong add the same day.

$.toolUseResult.annotations.Decision 3 of 4: what happens when a broker exports?

Recommendation: every export is frozen automatically (the xlsx plus a data JSON go to S3, and a row is added to "Exported reports"). A broker who later asks "what did we send?" always has the answer, and storage is negligible. The cost is that trial exports also appear in the list, labelled by time and period. The alternative adds a separate "Mark as sent" step that brokers will forget.
